docs.title: GLAPAGOS Technical Architecture
docs.text: Version 1.0 | Working Document

docs.title: Design Goals
docs.text:
The architecture satisfies the following constraints derived from the mission and governance requirements.

Federated, not centralized: No single node controls the system. Any member institution must be able to run a local instance that interoperates with the global network without depending on any single infrastructure provider.

Auditable: Every significant action is logged with sufficient context for independent review. Logs are tamper-evident.

Multilingual from the ground up: The API, data schemas, documentation, and interfaces support multiple languages without retrofitting. Language is a first-class concern.

Modular: Components can be deployed and used independently. A researcher who only needs the benchmark suite should not need to deploy the full platform.

Long-lived: The architecture anticipates operation over decades. Dependencies are chosen for stability. Breaking changes are versioned and migrated, not dropped.

docs.title: Core Platform Layer
docs.text:
Provides foundational services all other components depend on.

src/core/
  auth/       Authentication and authorization (OAuth2, API keys, SSO)
  registry/   Module, model, and dataset registry
  audit/      Tamper-evident audit logging
  federation/ Federated instance discovery and communication
  storage/    Abstracted storage interface (local, S3-compatible)
  i18n/       Internationalization utilities

The core layer has no AI-specific dependencies. It is a general platform for open, federated scientific collaboration.

docs.title: API Layer
docs.text:
Exposes platform capabilities over HTTP. Follows REST conventions with OpenAPI 3.1 specification.

src/api/
  v1/
    health/     Health and readiness endpoints
    registry/   Module, model, dataset registry endpoints
    research/   Research submission and retrieval
    governance/ Governance record access
    federation/ Inter-instance communication

API versioning is explicit in the URL path. Breaking changes require a new major version.

docs.title: SDK Layer
docs.text:
Language-specific client libraries for interacting with the GLAPAGOS API and local tools.

src/sdk/
  python/     Python SDK (primary)
  typescript/ TypeScript SDK

docs.title: CLI Layer
docs.text:
Terminal access to all SDK functionality.

src/cli/
  main.py
  commands/
    registry  Model, dataset, module registry commands
    bench     Benchmark commands
    publish   Publication commands
    config    Configuration management

docs.title: Data Commons
docs.text:
The Data Commons is a governed repository of open datasets. It is not a centralized database. It is a specification for how datasets are documented, indexed, and accessed.

Each dataset has: - A machine-readable manifest (manifest.json) - A provenance record tracing data origin, collection, and consent - A governance record with applicable licenses and restrictions - Integrity checksums for all files

Datasets are stored in contributors' infrastructure and indexed by the GLAPAGOS registry. This prevents single-point-of-failure and respects data residency requirements.

docs.title: Indigenous Data Protocol
docs.text:
Data originating from or pertaining to Indigenous communities requires: - Free, prior, and informed consent documented before contribution - Ongoing benefit-sharing mechanism documented in the manifest - Community right to withdrawal for future use - No aggregation with non-consented data

This is an architectural requirement enforced in the contribution pipeline, not an optional policy.

docs.title: Model Registry
docs.text: Registry entries include: - Model card following the Americas AI Model Card standard - Benchmark results from at least one GLAPAGOS benchmark - License and usage terms - Known limitations and failure modes - Dependency manifest (training data, base models, compute)

docs.title: Benchmark Suite
docs.text:
Initial benchmark domains: - AMER-LANG: Multilingual language understanding - AMER-CULT: Cultural knowledge and representation - AMER-SAFE: Safety evaluation for hemisphere-specific contexts - AMER-CIVIC: Civic knowledge and reasoning across jurisdictions

Benchmarks are versioned. Comparisons must reference the same version.

docs.title: Federation Architecture
docs.text:
GLAPAGOS runs as a network of federated instances. A member institution can run its own instance that: - Maintains local copies of relevant registry entries - Contributes locally hosted datasets and models to the global registry - Runs benchmarks on local compute - Participates in governance through the API

The federation protocol is published and open.

docs.title: Security Architecture
docs.text:
Authentication: OAuth2 with PKCE for human users. API key for machine clients with rotation requirements. SAML2/OIDC for institutional SSO. All tokens are short-lived.

Audit Logging: Append-only log with cryptographic chaining. Each entry includes the hash of the previous entry, making retrospective modification detectable.

Supply Chain: All dependencies pinned by version and hash. SBOM generated on every release. Container images are signed.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
Reference deployment uses infrastructure available from multiple cloud providers, documented in infrastructure/terraform/. Cloud-provider- agnostic by design.

Required infrastructure: - Containerized API and worker services (Docker, Kubernetes) - Relational database (PostgreSQL 15+) - Object storage (S3-compatible) - Reverse proxy and TLS termination

Estimated cost for reference deployment: $500-1500/month depending on load, or equivalent on institutional on-premises hardware.

Full local development requires only Docker and Docker Compose. Run make docker-up to start all required services.

This document is maintained alongside the GLAPAGOS codebase. Implementation status is tracked in GitHub Issues.

docs.title: Institution Engagement Guide
docs.text:
This document provides a structured approach to engaging research institutions, governments, universities, multilateral organizations, and other stakeholders in GLAPAGOS.

This is not a marketing document. The credibility of GLAPAGOS depends on the quality of its work and governance. This guide focuses on creating conditions under which serious organizations find participation professionally valuable.

docs.title: Credibility Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before active outreach, the following must be in place. Attempting to recruit institutions without them will undermine long-term credibility.

Technical prerequisites: - Repository is publicly available and demonstrates serious engineering - CI/CD pipelines are operational and all checks pass - At least one functional software artifact is released - Documentation is complete and accurate - Security policy is in place

Governance prerequisites: - Constitution and Governance Framework are published - Ethics and Governance Board composition process is documented - Conflict of interest policy is documented and enforced - Financial transparency policy is documented

Research prerequisites: - At least one substantive technical output published - Publication policy is documented - Research ethics process is documented

Do not skip these prerequisites. Institutions asked to join before these are in place will, and should, decline.

docs.title: Research Universities
docs.text:
What they need: Credible research outputs, legitimate governance, publication opportunities, student and faculty engagement pathways.

Approach: - Identify the relevant research center or department - Contact the research center director or relevant faculty, not university administration - Propose a specific, concrete form of engagement - Send documentation a researcher would find credible: the technical white paper, architecture document, and governance framework - Do not lead with membership fees. Lead with research value.

docs.title: Government Bodies
docs.text:
What they need: Clear policy relevance, legal compatibility with their mandate, governance representing their interests without compromising sovereignty, low administrative burden.

Approach: - Identify the relevant ministry (technology, digital transformation, science) - Contact at director or policy specialist level initially - Frame participation in terms of policy outcomes - Emphasize the non-binding nature of observer participation - Be explicit about sovereignty provisions in the Constitution

docs.title: Multilateral Organizations
docs.text:
IDB: Active AI and digital economy programming. Target the Digital Economy Division and Innovation Laboratory. Frame around compute infrastructure investment and AI governance standards.

UNDP Digital 4 Development Hub LAC: Explicitly coordinates inclusive digitalization. Target the Hub coordinator directly. Frame around their country office mandate.

CAF: Co-funded LATAM-GPT. Has infrastructure investment capacity. Target the innovation or digital economy team.

docs.title: Civil Society Organizations
docs.text:
What they need: Mission alignment, trustworthy governance, low financial barriers, genuine voice in decisions.

Approach: - Waive or substantially reduce membership fees - Ensure Working Groups genuinely include civil society perspectives - Be explicit that civil society participation is substantive

docs.title: The Outreach Sequence
docs.text:
For any institution, the recommended sequence is:

  1. Desk research: Understand the institution's mission, current AI activities, and relevant staff before contacting them.

  2. Initial contact: A concise, specific communication from a named individual with a relevant credential. Include specific reasons why this institution's participation would be valuable and what GLAPAGOS offers them.

  3. Documentation sharing: Share technical and governance documentation.

  4. Meeting or call: Focus on their questions and concerns.

  5. Concrete next step: Propose a specific, low-commitment engagement. Not membership. One Working Group meeting, one document review, one benchmark co-authorship.

  6. Membership discussion: After concrete engagement has demonstrated value, discuss formal membership.

docs.title: Building Research Credibility
docs.text:
The fastest path to credibility is publishing work that researchers find valuable.

Benchmark releases: A well-designed benchmark for multilingual AI evaluation will be cited and used. It establishes expertise without requiring large compute.

Dataset contributions: A documented, governed dataset with clear provenance fills a gap researchers can point to.

Technical reports: Analysis of AI governance frameworks across the hemisphere, comparison of regulatory approaches, or documentation of AI deployment challenges in specific sectors.

Open workshops: Invite relevant researchers to a workshop focused on a specific technical problem. Publish the outputs.

docs.title: Community Health Metrics
docs.text:
Track and publish annually: - Member institutions by country and category - Individual contributors by country and domain - Research outputs published - Working Group participation (unique attendees, affiliation diversity) - Benchmark adoptions by external researchers - Dataset downloads - Governance decision response times - Ethics and Governance Board findings and responses

These metrics demonstrate institutional health to potential partners and funders. They also identify problems early.

docs.title: AI Bill of Rights for the Americas
Draft Framework for Public Comment
docs.text:
Status: Draft | Working Group: WG-GOV | Version: 0.1.0

This document is a working draft published for community comment. It is not yet adopted policy. To comment, open a GitHub Issue with label wg-gov or attend WG-GOV monthly meetings.

The framework draws on the U.S. Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights, the EU AI Act, UNESCO's Recommendation on the Ethics of AI, and H.Res. 649 (118th Congress), adapted for the Western Hemisphere.

docs.title: Preamble
docs.text:
The nations and peoples of the Western Hemisphere affirm the following rights as applicable to all persons interacting with or affected by AI systems in the Americas.

These rights are principles for voluntary adoption and incorporation into national and regional regulatory frameworks. They are not self-executing legal obligations.

docs.title: Right 1: Safe and Effective Systems
docs.text:
You should be protected from unsafe or ineffective AI systems.

AI systems should be designed, developed, and deployed to be safe and effective for their intended use. Before deployment in consequential contexts, AI systems should be tested to verify they perform as intended without undue risk.

Americas context: Testing must include evaluation on Spanish, Portuguese, French, Haitian Creole, and other widely spoken hemisphere languages. Systems affecting Indigenous communities must be evaluated for cultural safety in those communities' contexts.

docs.title: Right 2: Algorithmic Non-Discrimination
docs.text:
You should not face discrimination from AI systems.

AI systems must not discriminate based on race, color, ethnicity, national origin, language, gender, age, disability, religion, socioeconomic status, geographic location, or other protected characteristics, including through ostensibly neutral criteria that produce disparate effects.

Americas context: The significant demographic diversity of the Americas, including Indigenous, Afro-descendant, immigrant, and economically marginalized communities, creates specific discrimination risks. AI in consequential domains must be evaluated for disparate impact.

docs.title: Right 3: Transparency and Notice
docs.text:
You should know when AI is being used in decisions affecting you.

Where AI makes or substantially contributes to a decision affecting an individual's rights, opportunities, or access to services, the individual should be informed that AI was used, what it was designed to do, and what data was used.

Americas context: Disclosure must be in a language the affected person understands. English-only disclosure is insufficient where the affected population primarily speaks other languages.

docs.title: Right 4: Explanation
docs.text:
You should be able to understand decisions affecting you.

Where AI substantially contributes to a consequential decision, the affected individual has the right to a meaningful plain-language explanation of how that decision was reached.

docs.title: Right 5: Human Alternatives
docs.text:
You should not be denied access to a human decision-maker.

AI systems should not eliminate entirely the availability of human review in consequential decisions. Individuals who prefer human review should be able to access it within a reasonable time.

docs.title: Right 6: Data Privacy and Autonomy
docs.text:
You should have control over your data.

Individuals have the right to know what data is collected about them, for what purposes, to access and correct that data, and to request deletion where there is no overriding public interest in retention.

docs.title: Right 7: Contestability
docs.text:
You have rights regarding automated decisions.

Where automated systems make decisions with no meaningful human involvement, affected individuals have the right to know the decision was automated, receive an explanation, contest it through a human review process, and seek recourse for harm.

docs.title: Right 8: Human Oversight
docs.text:
AI systems in the public interest require meaningful human oversight.

AI deployed by governments or in public services must operate under oversight where humans can monitor behavior, intervene when AI acts inconsistently with its intended purpose or applicable law, and are accountable for consequences.

docs.title: Implementation Framework
docs.text:
Pre-deployment assessment: Developers and deployers should conduct and publish an assessment covering intended use, affected populations, data used, known limitations, evaluation results, and planned monitoring.

Ongoing monitoring: Deployed systems should be monitored for performance, disparate impact, and unexpected behavior.

Incident reporting: Significant AI incidents should be reported and investigated. GLAPAGOS maintains a voluntary incident registry.

Comments accepted via GitHub Issues (label: wg-gov) or at WG-GOV monthly meetings. See community/councils/wg-gov/ for schedule.
